synthesis: The scheduled cache-warm job for hotlist client/lienholder dropdowns (App\Jobs\Org\CacheOrgHotlistClients / CacheOrgHotlistLienholders, driven by GenerateOrgCache every 4h) repeatedly hits a Postgres statement_timeout (SQLSTATE 57014) on the zod read replica while running `SELECT name,id FROM orgs WHERE id IN (SELECT DISTINCT client_org_id FROM hotlist WHERE org_id=? AND client_org_id IS NOT NULL) ORDER BY name`. Because the query throws before cache()->remember() reaches put(), no value is ever stored, so the cache stays cold and the identical expensive query re-runs on every 4h tick AND on every synchronous UI call that falls through on a cache miss (8 Filament call sites). Critically, this exact query shape is what DEV-1898 (Done, commit c744f887) already shipped as 'the fix' for the sibling ticket -- it pushed DISTINCT + WHERE NOT NULL into the SQL subquery and removed the old PHP-side pluck()->unique(). DEV-2220 is the recurrence after that fix, which proves the query-rewrite alone was insufficient; the residual cost lives in missing index coverage (no composite (org_id,client_org_id)/(org_id,lienholder_org_id) index exists on public.hotlist) and possibly table-level factors (autovacuum is explicitly disabled on public.hotlist) that are outside this query's control. Desired outcome: stop the repeated statement-timeout failures/noise and make the two cache-warm paths degrade safely (and, ideally, get the cache to actually populate) -- while being honest that the durable fix (an index) is schema/vendor-owned and cannot be delivered from a platform-only PR.

scope.summary: Given DEV-1898 already did the SQL-side rewrite and it still times out, and given the composite index that would actually fix the query lives in the vendor-owned zod schema (platform's own zod-connection migrations are guarded off in production), the realistic platform-only scope is resilience/graceful-degradation: catch the specific timeout in Org::getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders() (not just the job wrapper, since 8 Filament call sites invoke these methods synchronously and would otherwise surface a raw timeout to users), log/metric it with org_id context using the repo's existing QueryException-handling conventions, and fall back to an empty Collection instead of throwing -- matching the precedent already used by the sibling StagingOrgsHotlistCount::getCount(). The composite index (the ticket's actual root-cause hint) is called out explicitly as a cross-repo/ops dependency, not something this PR can ship to production.

proposed_changes.change: Wrap the cache()->remember() closure body in getHotlistClients() (line 185) in a try/catch for Illuminate\Database\QueryException (SQLSTATE 57014 / 'statement timeout'), log via the existing Log::channel('db-error') + logDatadogCount('clarity.query_timeout', ...) pattern with org_id context, and return an empty Collection on catch instead of letting the exception propagate.
proposed_changes.reason: Prevents the timeout from surfacing as a raw 500/exception to every synchronous UI caller (HitsResource, HotlistResource, MissedOpportunityResource, ClientTable, AlertSettingsForm, IndividualClientAnalytics, CreateMissedOpportunityAlertSettings) when the cache is cold, matching the existing repo convention in StagingOrgsHotlistCount::getCount().

proposed_changes.change: Apply the identical try/catch + empty-Collection-fallback treatment to getHotlistLienholders() (line 202).
proposed_changes.reason: Sibling method, identical failure mode, identical UI-call-site risk (MissedOpportunityResource, HitsResource).

proposed_changes.change: Add a test asserting the job completes without throwing when the underlying Hotlist subquery raises a QueryException, and that the resulting behavior (empty collection, no cache write vs. short-TTL negative cache -- pending the open question below) matches whatever the implementation lands on.
proposed_changes.reason: Pins the new resilience behavior; existing tests only cover the happy path.

proposed_changes.change: Same addition as above for the lienholders job.

out_of_scope: Adding the composite (org_id,client_org_id) / (org_id,lienholder_org_id) index to public.hotlist from this repo -- schema/index ownership lives in insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations, and platform's only zod-connection migration (2025_08_06_124727_add_plate_variants_function.php) is guarded `config('app.env') !== 'production'`, so a platform migration would be a no-op in prod. Needs a companion PR to laravel-zod-migrations (+ composer bump) or a direct DBA-run CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY against the production primary.

Reshaping the query into an explicit JOIN/EXISTS -- Postgres's planner already treats IN(DISTINCT subquery) as an equivalent semi-join in typical cases, so this is unlikely to change the plan without the index, and verifying that requires EXPLAIN ANALYZE against production-scale data this repo/environment doesn't have.

Forcing the write/primary connection for this query (useWritePdo()) -- unconfirmed whether the replica has a stricter statement_timeout than the primary (not configured anywhere in this repo; it's a Postgres server/role GUC), and would add read load to the primary for a bulk background job across all active orgs.

Any change to public.hotlist's autovacuum/bloat maintenance cadence (table has autovacuum_enabled='false' set at the storage-parameter level) -- external ops/vendor concern, not visible or actionable from this repo.
Changing GenerateOrgCache's schedule cadence, queue, or batch structure.
The broader DEV-2202 epic rollup of other read-replica timeout jobs -- only the two hotlist-client/lienholder methods named in this ticket are in scope.

acceptance_criteria.item: CacheOrgHotlistClients / CacheOrgHotlistLienholders no longer let an uncaught QueryException propagate on statement timeout.
acceptance_criteria.reason: Directly addresses the ticket's stated symptom (dominant error, 12x/20x per day) and is achievable within platform.

acceptance_criteria.item: getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders() degrade to an empty Collection (not a 500/exception) when the underlying query times out, for both the cron job and the 8 synchronous Filament call sites.
acceptance_criteria.reason: The methods are called synchronously from UI code, not just the warm job; matches existing StagingOrgsHotlistCount::getCount() fallback convention.

acceptance_criteria.item: Statement-timeout occurrences are logged/metriced with org_id context so affected orgs can be identified.
acceptance_criteria.reason: The existing global reporter in bootstrap/app.php only counts a generic Datadog metric with no org context; HasRetryQuery.php shows the repo's convention for richer contextual logging.

acceptance_criteria.item: Add a composite index on public.hotlist covering (org_id, client_org_id) and (org_id, lienholder_org_id).
acceptance_criteria.reason: Schema/index ownership lives in the vendor package insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations; platform's own zod migrations are guarded off in production and cannot deliver this. Needs a cross-repo PR or direct DBA action -- tracked as a follow-up, not part of this PR.

acceptance_criteria.item: Rewrite the query as an explicit JOIN/EXISTS instead of whereIn(subquery).
acceptance_criteria.reason: Current shape is already what DEV-1898 produced; without the index, a JOIN/EXISTS reshape is unlikely to change the plan, and this can't be confirmed without EXPLAIN ANALYZE against production-scale data.

acceptance_criteria.item: Move the query off the read replica / onto a per-statement bounded timeout.
acceptance_criteria.reason: statement_timeout is not configured anywhere in this repo (confirmed via repo-wide grep) -- it's an external Postgres GUC. Whether the replica's timeout differs from the primary's is unknown from code; needs DBA confirmation before considering useWritePdo() or a SET LOCAL statement_timeout mitigation.

questions.q: Is a composite covering index the accepted durable fix, and who/where executes it -- a companion PR to insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations (+ composer bump), or a direct DBA-run CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY against the production primary (which would replicate to the read replica automatically)?

Should getHotlistClients()/getHotlistLienholders() also write a short-TTL negative cache (e.g., an empty Collection cached for 10-15 min) on failure to bound repeated replica load between cache-miss calls, or is a plain try/catch per call (re-attempting the expensive query on every single request/tick) sufficient?
Does the zod read replica enforce a stricter statement_timeout than the write/primary connection?

Does public.hotlist's autovacuum_enabled='false' storage parameter (confirmed in vendor zod-schema.sql:3985) imply a manual VACUUM/ANALYZE cadence exists in production, and could missed/lapsed vacuuming be contributing to the slow heap fetches behind this timeout?
Is the pre-existing whereNotNull('client_org_id') call in getHotlistClients() (Org.php:193) worth removing as dead code, given client_org_id is NOT NULL at the schema level?
questions.answer: It's a functional no-op (harmless, filters nothing) since public.hotlist.client_org_id is declared NOT NULL in the vendor schema (zod-schema.sql:3971). Safe to leave or remove; not load-bearing either way.

blockers: The durable root-cause fix (composite index on public.hotlist) cannot be shipped to production from this repo alone: the table/index set is owned by the external insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations package, and platform's only zod-connection migration is guarded to non-production. This does not block the mitigation-only scope above, but it does block actually resolving the timeout for the large/skewed orgs that are hitting it.
notes: DEV-1898 (commit c744f887) already pushed DISTINCT + WHERE NOT NULL into the hotlist subquery and removed the old PHP-side pluck()->unique() for both getHotlistClients() and getHotlistLienholders() -- that is exactly today's code. DEV-2220 is the recurrence after that fix, confirming the query rewrite alone was insufficient (expected, since it didn't add an index).

public.hotlist has autovacuum_enabled='false' set at the table storage-parameter level (vendor zod-schema.sql:3985), meaning bloat/dead-tuple management for this specific table is entirely manual/external -- a plausible (unconfirmed) contributing factor to slow heap fetches getting worse over time.

hotlist.org_id has SET STATISTICS 5000 (vendor zod-schema.sql:3986) -- a DBA already tuned stats on this column, consistent with known per-org row-count skew; the timeout is very plausibly concentrated on a handful of large orgs rather than uniform across all orgs.
Existing repo precedent for 'swallow QueryException on cache-miss, fall back to empty/zero' already exists: StagingOrgsHotlistCount::getCount() (app/Models/Views/StagingOrgsHotlistCount.php:26-34).

Existing repo precedent for structured QueryException logging + Datadog metric on a query-timeout: app/Filament/Concerns/HasRetryQuery.php (Log::channel('db-error') + logDatadogCount('clarity.query_timeout', ...)).

A repo-wide exception reporter already exists in bootstrap/app.php:20-29 that increments a generic clarity.query_timeout Datadog metric for ANY uncaught QueryException matching SQLSTATE 57014 / 'statement timeout' -- this is almost certainly how the ticket's 12x/20x counts were observed. It does not suppress default logging/reporting and carries no org_id context, so today's noise is neither deduplicated nor attributable to a specific org.

config/database.php's zod connection (lines 58-73) has no 'sticky' key (unlike platform/pg/graphql, which default sticky=true) -- reads always go to DB_READ_HOST regardless of recent writes on this connection, consistent with the ticket's 'read replica' framing.

Horizon's {low} queue supervisor has tries=1 (config/horizon.php:205) -- a failed job is not auto-retried by the queue itself; the repeated failures are driven entirely by GenerateOrgCache's everyFourHours() schedule (routes/console.php:19-22) re-dispatching a fresh batch every tick, matching the ticket's 00/04/08/12/16/20 cadence.

Test approach: forcing a genuine SQLSTATE 57014 in the local/CI Postgres test DB isn't practical (no realistic data volume to trigger a real timeout); the added tests should exercise the catch path via a partial mock of the query builder / a forced QueryException, not a real timeout.
Pint/style: any new catch block should follow the repo's curly-brace-always + explicit-return-type conventions already used throughout Org.php.

Subquery is an eager pluck() over `shared` (small pivot-like table), not whereIn(subquery-with-DISTINCT) over hotlist-scale data.

ApprovalList::query()->where('agent_org_id',...)->pluck(...) -- no whereIn(subquery), smaller table, no reported skew/timeout.

Calls getRdnClients() (external API, no DB risk).
No whereIn(subquery)/cache-warm-of-a-large-table pattern; operates on the org's own runArea relation.

reasons: The ticket's own triage hints (composite index, query reshape, read-replica routing) are all either cross-repo, unconfirmed from this repo alone, or genuinely require a DBA -- this is real option-space that a best-of-N reconcile would sharpen, not manufactured ambiguity.

Cross-repo dependency: the durable fix needs a companion change in insight-lpr/laravel-zod-migrations and/or direct DBA action against production Postgres; platform's own zod migrations are guarded off in production and cannot deliver it.

Four open questions genuinely need a human/DBA decision (index execution path, negative-cache UX tradeoff, replica vs primary statement_timeout, autovacuum/bloat cadence) before the mitigation-only scope can be called complete.
